title: Socialist Republic of Romania
capsule: Communist Romania spanned the whole of this window (1948-1990). The Romanian People's Republic was proclaimed on 30 December 1947 after King Michael's forced abdication and entrenched by the April 1948 constitution; under Gheorghe Gheorghiu-Dej the regime imposed Stalinist consolidation, mass arrests and the Securitate through the 1950s while gradually asserting distance from Moscow, securing the withdrawal of Soviet troops in 1958. On 21 August 1965 Nicolae Ceausescu renamed the state the Socialist Republic of Romania and built a personalist nationalist communism, refusing to join the 1968 Warsaw Pact invasion of Czechoslovakia and winning temporary Western goodwill. His 1980s drive to repay foreign debt in full brought severe food and energy shortages, and the regime collapsed in the December 1989 revolution: Ceausescu and his wife Elena were tried and executed on 25 December 1989, after which the country reverted to the name Romania.
